assessed_by: commit + config read; no differential run (correctly, see why_excluded)

discovery.found_by: one of only 4 library_confirmed rows among 66 unread needs_reading rows in the adaptation corpus

the_candidate.message: Set maxStringLength in Jackson JsonFactory to maxResponseSize in HttpClient.
the_candidate.shape: A — the HttpClient(config, provider, objectMapper, ...) constructor existed at the parent; the diff only added lines inside it

traversal.ancestry: GitHub compare b1ea07d9...6f06ced3 returns status=ahead, behind_by=0, so the bump is an ancestor of the adaptation, two commits earlier on the same day
traversal.note: THE PIPELINE GOT THIS WRONG. bbc_e2e traversal returned 'no boundary-crossing bump in the adaptation's ancestry (client was born at/above the boundary)'. See traversal_bug below.

why_excluded.finding: The adaptation sets jackson's string limit BELOW jackson's own 2.15 default, so it tightens rather than restores. No input can produce pass/fail/pass.
why_excluded.the_code: HttpClient's constructor gains: StreamReadConstraints.builder().maxStringLength(config.getMaxResponseSize()).build(), installed on this.objectMapper.getFactory().
why_excluded.the_decisive_number: HttpClientConfig.maxResponseSize defaults to 10 * 1024 * 1024 = 10,485,760. StreamReadConstraints.DEFAULT_MAX_STRING_LEN at 2.15 is 20,000,000. The configured limit is therefore roughly HALF the library default.

size_analysis.<= 10,485,760: state 1 pass / state 2 pass / state 3 pass
size_analysis.10,485,760 - 20,000,000: state 1 pass / state 2 pass / state 3 FAIL
size_analysis.> 20,000,000: state 1 pass / state 2 FAIL / state 3 FAIL

why_excluded.conclusion: There is no string length for which the baseline passes, the unadapted new version fails, and the adapted version passes. The oracle has nothing to detect.
why_excluded.why_the_classifier_could_not_score_it: find_adaptations scored this needs_reading because the value is a variable, config.getMaxResponseSize(), not a literal. resolve_variable only follows assignments within the same diff, and this one resolves in a different file. A raise/lower verdict here required reading HttpClientConfig.

traversal_bug.symptom: traversal reported 'born at/above the boundary' -- a confident MEASURED negative -- for a client that demonstrably crossed 2.14.2 -> 2.15.0 two commits earlier.
traversal_bug.cause: The break is keyed on com.fasterxml.jackson.core:jackson-core. This client declares com.fasterxml.jackson:jackson-bom and sets <jackson-bom.version>. dep_version never matches the coordinate, so no build file yields a version at any commit, and the walk concludes the client was always at/above the boundary instead of reporting that it could not resolve anything.
traversal_bug.severity: A failure to measure rendered as a measurement -- the same class of defect as the pre-2026-08-03 traversal bug recorded in the corpus. Any client declaring a BOM (jackson-bom, spring-boot-dependencies) or a sibling artifact (jackson-databind, jackson-dataformat-yaml) is affected.
traversal_bug.known_affected: Of nine born-past dispositions made on 2026-08-16, only vdaburon/har-to-jmeter-convertor declares jackson-core directly. mkarjun/LCS declares jackson-bom and jackson-databind; OussamaLakhdar90/veritas declares jackson-dataformat-yaml; mmaudet/eu-dss-module uses a property plus the spring-boot BOM. All must be re-checked.

value: Two independent findings from one candidate. The client is not a case, and the reason was one integer in a config class -- an hour of reading instead of a day of driver work. And the pipeline's traversal is provably capable of a confident false negative, which is worth more than the candidate would have been.
